content.text:
Let me work through this ticket.

Employee: Morgan Swanson (E037), requests write access to Payroll.

Access levels: none, read, write, admin.

HR note: full-time Engineer, recommends write for Payroll (full-time max write, role doesn't own Payroll so no admin).

Security note: contractor with basic security training, recommends read (contractor max read unless advanced training; write requires advanced training).

Conflict: HR says full-time, security says contractor. Security note says "security record takes precedence."

Policy:
- full_time: up to write. Admin only if role owns system. Engineer doesn't own Payroll.
- contractor: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

If full-time: requested write ≤ max write → grant write.
If contractor with basic training: max read → requested write above max → grant read.

The two notes disagree on employment type. The security note states security record takes precedence. As Approver, which to use? The notes are evidence. The security agent notes that employment type discrepancy and says security record takes precedence. Typically, security database is authoritative for contractor status. So the employee is a contractor with basic training. Max = read. Requested write > read, grant read.

So decision: read.

Let me submit with reasoning.
